alex: quick design sanity check — putting up a couple of delete/validation options in figma for the pipelines list: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz (see 'compact delete' + 'typed confirm' frames) alex: tl;dr: option A = compact modal with typed-confirm (type the resource name) + strong warning. option B = soft-delete + global snackbar undo + inline error surfacing for form fixes. which direction feels safer/easier to scan? maria: typed-confirm is high friction but very explicit. +1 for safety on destructive ops if this is customer-data destructive. maria: also: if we force typing, we should surface what exact string expected (case? id?) — that copy must be clear. sam: i'm worried about interruption with typed confirm for quick workflows. for bulk deletes it could be OK, but for single accidental click, snackbar undo is less catastrophic and less mental load. jordan: accessibility note: typed-confirm can be problematic for screen-reader users if not implemented with proper aria-describedby and live-region confirmations. typing the exact name can be hard depending on name complexity. jordan: suggestion: if we go typed-confirm, add an aria-live polite region that repeats the instruction and the expected text, and ensure the confirmation input has aria-label and autocomplete=off. lee: regarding required markers — proposal in figma uses an asterisk plus 'required' hint on hover. i'm leaning to explicit "(required)" label for complex forms, but asterisk is fine for compact lists. lee: also we should not rely only on color to indicate required or error states. alex: good point. for the long-create pipeline form, thinking: inline errors next to fields + a small top summary that only appears when there are more than 2 errors. keeps focus but still gives overview. maria: agree. summary only when needed. top summary should link to first error and list field names. sam: small UX nit — when showing inline errors, keep copy short (1 line) and show example valid value if helpful. avoid full sentences in-line. alex: ok — for destructive flow would folks accept hybrid: show typed-confirm for >5 items or when selecting datasets flagged as 'sensitive', otherwise soft-delete + undo snackbar? jordan: hybrid makes sense. we should surface reason for typed requirement: "This dataset contains sensitive PII — typing the name prevents accidental loss." make sure that text is programmatic so we can A/B toggle. lee: can we add a brief code snippet for the aria-live approach? here's a draft: ```
Type the pipeline name to confirm deletion.
``` lee: also add role="status" to the snackbar for SRs. alex: nice. last question: required marker style — asterisk + inline '(required)' in tooltips? or explicit text appended to label for first-pass? maria: explicit '(required)' for first-pass on long forms. asterisk on condensed views. consistency doc callout in design system. sam: +1 to consistency. also record examples in the components page. design-bot: reminder — please add a11y check to the PR checklist: "confirm keyboard/voiceover flow for typed confirm and snackbar undo" :bookmark_tabs: alex: thanks everyone. i'll update figma with hybrid rules (typed-confirm triggers) and a11y notes, then prototype the snackbar undo microcopy. want to run a quick hallway test after that. :thumbsup:
